Context from your recent conversation:

## Baseline Memory Profile
These are remembered facts about the person. They never set the reply language.
- about_you (global): I live in Dublin.
- about_you (global): I prefer concise answers.

## Current User Message
Segíts kitalálni, hova menjünk idén nyáron nyaralni.

## Turn Guidance
[SYSTEM TIME CONTEXT: Today is Thursday, November 5, 2026. Use this exact date as your current temporal anchor for relative timeframes. Call a date/time tool only when exact current time, timezone, or freshness-sensitive tool behavior materially depends on it.]

Reply in the language of the person's latest message, judged by its own words.
If that message has no language of its own (a short "ok", a number, a link, code), keep the language they have been writing in.
If they ask for the reply in a particular language, in this message or in their standing instructions (Your Instructions, Project Instructions), use that.
If they ask for a piece of writing in another language (an email, a translation), write that piece in it and keep your own words in their language.
Nothing else sets the reply language: not who they are (their name, nationality or where they live), not remembered facts (even one about the language they use), documents, files, tool or search results, or your own earlier replies.

Reasoning depth effort profile:
- Applied Normal Chat profile: standard. This does not force web search every turn, and does not make the visible answer longer by itself.
Standard-depth reasoning contract:
- Use normal private reasoning. Keep the answer efficient, but still check obvious constraints and avoid unsupported claims.
- Grounding pressure: standard. Use retrieval when the ordinary web/source guidance says it is needed.
- Tool loop budget: the runtime can support up to 14 tool steps for this profile. Stop early once the answer is grounded enough.

## Skills available
- Plan Critic — Finds the blockers, weak assumptions, and gaps in a plan before you execute it, ranked by severity.
- Document Explainer — Explains an attached or linked document in plain language, preserving exact numbers, dates, and caveats — fetches a URL first if you paste one.
- Study Coach — Coaches active learning with chunked explanations, recall questions, and a study plan instead of a plain summary.
- Purchase Helper — Compares purchase options against your real constraints and current prices — researches the web for specs and reviews before recommending.
- Translate & Rewrite — Translates or rewrites text while preserving meaning, tone, and exact terminology, names, and numbers.
- Appointment Prep — Builds an agenda, questions, and a verify/flag checklist for an upcoming appointment or call — pulls in prior context automatically.
- Spreadsheet Builder — Builds polished XLSX workbooks with real formulas, formatted tables, and dashboards, delivered as a downloadable file.

## Drafting a skill
When the person asks you to keep how you just worked as a reusable skill ("make this a skill", "save this as a skill"), draft it in this block at the end of the reply, with no text inside it:

<skill_control_v1>
{"version":1,"operations":[{"operationId":"skill-draft-1","kind":"skill_draft","draft":{"id":"weekly-status","displayName":"Weekly status","description":"Writes a short weekly status update from what the conversation already says.","instructions":"Ask for the period, then write one short paragraph: what is done, what is next, what blocks it.","activationExamples":["Write my weekly status."],"sourceScope":"current_conversation"}}]}
</skill_control_v1>

The app removes the block before the person sees the reply and shows a card with Save private skill and Dismiss: the skill exists only after they save it, so never claim it is saved. The example's `id`, `displayName` and `instructions` are only the shape: write them for the skill the person asked for, with `activationExamples` as messages that should load it.

response.thinking:
A felhasználó magyarul kérdez: "Segíts kitalálni, hova menjünk idén nyáron nyaralni." — Segíts kitalálni, hova menjünk idén nyáron nyaralni.

Today is November 5, 2026. "Idén nyáron" = this summer — but summer 2026 has already passed (June-August 2026). Hmm, November 2026 → "this year's summer" would be summer 2026, which is past. Possibly they mean next summer (2027). This is a genuine ambiguity worth flagging/asking. Actually in Hungarian, "idén nyáron" strictly means this year's summer = summer 2026, which is already over. So likely they mean next summer, 2027. I should note that briefly.

The request is open-ended: help figure out where to go. Missing key details: budget, duration, who's going, interests, departure from Dublin (they live in Dublin). Rather than a generic list, I should ask a few questions — this is a case where the choice is truly theirs. Use ask_user with 2-3 questions.

But also give something useful first? The guidance says ask follow-up when missing detail materially changes the answer. Here it does. I could give a short shortlist plus ask. Best: brief framing + ask_user with 3 questions: (1) which summer / when & how long, (2) budget, (3) vibe/type of trip. Keep concise (user prefers concise).

Language: Hungarian.

Let me ask 3 questions:
1. Mikor és mennyi idő? Options: június/elő/nyár közepe, 1 hét, 2 hét... Actually combine: "Mennyi időtok van?" options: 1 hét, 10 nap, 2 hét, rugalmas.
2. Milyen típusú nyaralás? Options: tenger/part, városi kultúra, természet/aktív, laza mix.
3. Fejenkénti keret? Options: <500 €, 500–1000 €, 1000–2000 €, 2000 €+.
Also maybe: utazás repülővel Dublinból / autó+komp / nem számít.

Also flag the date issue: "idén nyár" már elmúlt (2026. nov 5), tehát 2027 nyarára tervezünk — ask that as question 1 maybe. Let me make question 1: "Melyik nyárra tervezel?" options: 2027 nyara (ajánlott), 2026 nyara már elmúlt... hmm awkward. Better: mention in prose one line, and ask about timing within summer.

I'll do: short prose noting 2026 nyara már mögöttünk, úgy értettem 2027 — javíts ki. Then ask_user with 3 questions. Mark recommended options where one-pick.

Note: ask_user pauses reply; I can include prose before the tool call. Then after they choose, I continue. Let me keep prose short.

Actually should I also give a couple of starter ideas to make it concrete? Keep it minimal — maybe 3 teaser directions tied to Dublin departures. But the answer continues after their choice anyway. A short line is fine.

Let me include options with notes.

Question 1: "Mennyi időtök van és mikor?" — multiple: false. Options: "1 hét, jun./szept." , "10 nap", "2 hét, nyár közepe (csúcs)", "Rugalmas, még nem tudom" (recommended? no). Hmm recommended only on one-pick question — mark one recommended per one-pick question? "Mark exactly one option recommended on a one-pick question". So for each multiple:false question, mark exactly one recommended. Ok.

Q1 options:
- "1 hét, június eleje vagy szeptember" note: olcsóbb, kevesebb tömeg (recommended)
- "10 nap"
- "2 hét, július–augusztus" note: csúcsárak
- "Még rugalmas"

Q2 type (multiple: true maybe): "Milyen nyaralás kell idén?" options: tenger + laza, város + kultúra, természet + túrázás, gasztronómia/bor. multiple: true → no recommended required (any number with multiple: true).

Q3 budget per person: "<500 €", "500–1000 €", "1000–2000 €", "2000 € felett". one-pick, recommend one? I'd recommend "500–1000 €" maybe. Fine.

Maybe also who's traveling (kids?) — that matters. But max 3 questions. I'll fold "kivel" into... hmm. Budget + duration + type are the big three. Kids would change recommendations a lot. I could make Q3 about who/how instead of budget. I'll keep budget and mention "szólj, ha gyerekekkel mentek" in prose.

Let's do it.
